    💡 Key Takeaways
    • DxDiag is a handy and free resource for troubleshooting DirectX.
    • DirectX is Microsoft's proprietary set of programming tools that help computer applications, especially games, communicate with your graphics card, audio and input devices.
    • DxDiag is a windows utility that scans your computer, collects technical system information and reports on installed DirectX components and drivers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    DxDiag is a handy and free resource for troubleshooting DirectX.

    DirectX is Microsoft's proprietary set of programming tools that help computer applications, especially games, communicate with your graphics card, audio and input devices. It allows software and hardware to work together to render graphics, play sound and deliver interactive multimedia experiences. If an application requires a DirectX capability but your computer doesn't support it, the application may fail to launch or crash mid-operation. Identifying the exact source behind these problems can be tricky, as outdated DirectX software, corrupt video card drivers or faulty Windows configuration could be contributing factors. This is where Microsoft's built-in DirectX diagnostic tool (DxDiag) can prove helpful.

    DxDiag is a windows utility that scans your computer, collects technical system information and reports on installed DirectX components and drivers. The tool can be used as a convenient starting point to investigate graphics or audio-related issues. It can also generate a condensed text report that you can share with technical support persons for analysis. Understanding the capabilities and limitations of DxDiag can help you make informed decisions when troubleshooting sound, visual or application compatibility issues.

    According to recent reports, to run the built-in DirectX diagnostic tool, initiate the run command with the windows + R shortcut, then type "dxdiag" and press enter. You can also search for "dxdiag" in the Windows start menu and launch the utility from there. The DxDiag tool includes tabs for System, Display, Sound and Input. It is recommended to tick the "Check for WHQL digital signatures" checkbox to verify the integrity of installed drivers.

    According to recent reports, the System page includes details on your PC's motherboard, processor, memory and graphics card. It also displays the DirectX version installed on your computer. Meanwhile, the Display page offers a detailed overview of your graphics card, from driver version to supported DirectX features like Direct3D Acceleration and DirectX 12 Ultimate. Similarly, the Sound page includes information on connected audio devices and their driver details, while the Input page lists all IO devices, including your keyboard, mouse and other peripherals. Make sure to review the Notes section at the bottom of Display, Sound and Input pages, since it may list errors reported by DxDiag.

    In a recent development, can DxDiag tell if the DirectX on your computer is corrupted? While it can help identify complications with display, sound and input devices, DxDiag cannot conclusively determine or repair DirectX problems. Just because the utility displays a clean report, it doesn't necessarily rule out all hardware and game-specific issues that your computer might be experiencing.

    If DxDiag reports display, sound or IO errors, start by comparing the affected component's driver version to the latest driver available. In case of discrepancy, consider downloading and installing the latest driver from the manufacturer's official website. While Windows revision often include driver updates, they are not always guaranteed be up to date. This could potentially result in outdated or incompatible drivers causing game-specific challenges even when your hardware meets the recommended system requirements. In case of audio-specific issues, in addition to drivers, also consider verifying that you're using the correct playback device in the Windows sound panel. You may also want check if the affected application or game has a newly introduced update or patch addressing hardware-related bugs.

    According to recent reports, if none of these steps end up resolving your problem, you can try running the sfc /scannow command as a administrator to scan and repair system files. If errors persist even after following these troubleshooting steps, it's recommended to contact Microsoft support and share your DxDiag report to help them investigate graphics, audio or other compatibility concerns in your PC.

    • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
    • An Australian beauty firm that promotes “clean” ingredients “free from skin irritants” has been referred to state health regulators after appearing to offer cigarettes to guests at a beachside lip gloss launch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Copini Beauty referred to New South Wales health regulators, while federal government says it is ‘deeply concerned’.

    Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

    An Australian beauty firm that promotes “clean” ingredients “free from skin irritants” has been referred to state health regulators after appearing to offer cigarettes to guests at a beachside lip gloss launch.

    Photos from an event held earlier in November at a venue in Bondi, Sydney show what appears to be loose cigarettes without health warnings on a tiered silver platter alongside a bowl of lip glosses.

    “Celebrating the launch of our soft gloss with our community,” one post from the event shared by the Copini Beauty account on Instagram read, with an accompanying carousel of images showing what appeared to be cigarettes on display with Copini-branded match boxes, lipglosses and glasses of wine.

    The images are also featured in a highlight reel from the event on the official Instagram page for the brand.

    Copini is co-founded by influencer Casey James and product developer Carla McGraw.

    Sources indicate that under the Public Health (Tobacco and Other Products) Act 2023, advertising or promoting smoking or the use of tobacco products is prohibited. Both state and federal laws prohibit businesses offering, giving or distributing a free tobacco product.

    Any tobacco supplied must also meet strict product standards, such as displaying mandatory graphic health warnings. The cigarettes at the Copini launch do not appear to carry any health warnings on the filter as required, indicating they are illicit products. Buying or supplying illicit tobacco is illegal in Australia, regardless of the quantity.

    Cigarettes in Australia cannot legally carry brand logos. The cigarettes appear to carry the Manchester “sapphire blue” branding, one of the most common illicit tobacco products in Australia. They are considered unlabelled under Australian law because they do not carry official government health warnings and compliant packaging.

    A spokesperson for the NSW health minister, Ryan Park, stated of the event and images: “This has been referred to NSW health’s centre for regulation and enforcement.”.

    The centre works with state and federal authorities to regulate smoking products and has powers to inspect premises, seize illicit stock, concern fines and prosecute offenders.

    A spokesperson for the federal health department stated the government is “deeply concerned about advertising or promotion that glamorises smoking or the use of tobacco products, or helps normalise tobacco use, particularly where it might reach young people”.

    “There is no appropriate place for tobacco products to be used as a promotional prop or to make smoking appear fashionable or appealing,” the spokesperson noted.

    “The government strengthened Australia’s tobacco laws to reduce the visibility and normalisation of tobacco products and protect Australians from the harms of smoking.”.

    The spokesperson said allegations of non-compliance with laws are taken seriously, saying the maximum penalty for criminal advertising or sponsorship of tobacco under federal laws is $728,000 for an individual, or $7.2m for a manufacturer.

    Smoking accelerates ageing and causes more than 16,000 cases of cancer in Australia each year. The display of cigarettes at the launch appears to contradict Copini’s philosophy: “We’re 100% vegan, cruelty-free, and free from skin irritants and endocrine disruptors,” the website states, stating that “clean ingredients” are used in all products.

    The tech giant did not respond to requests for comment.

    It comes amid growing concerns about the use of cigarettes by brands, and in images of celebrities, especially online, with health experts warning it risks normalising and glamourising smoking.

    Becky Freeman, a professor of tobacco control with the University of Sydney, stated it was “shocking to see the resurgence” of smoking in pop culture and on red carpets.

    “But to see this really local example, in Bondi, shows this is not an international phenomena – it’s happening in a country like Australia where we have low smoking rates through strong regulations and health policies,” she stated.

    A upcoming draft deal omits any mention of how to phase out fossil fuels, in what campaigners call a step 'backwards' and a 'glaring regression'.

    Like in previous years, the climate summit has been extended until a consensus is reached.

    These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21:.

    Sources indicate that the shift to green tech is already in full swing, including electric cars, electric buses, solar panels and heat pumps. But what is so electrifying about the latest wave of electrification?

    Harjeet Singh, the global convener of the Fill the Fund campaign and strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, stated that COP31 could be a failure due to a lack of funding.

    "COP31 is stuck for one simple reason: money. Europe and other rich countries came to Antalya with empty pockets," he wrote in a statement shared with multiple reporters.

    "They've spent two weeks pushing electrification targets and demanding more ambition from developing countries, while refusing to pay for any of it," he added.

    Singh accused wealthy countries of blocking a just transition mechanism and of ignoring calls to increase funding for the Adaptation Fund and the Loss and Damage Fund.

    "You can't ask developing countries to transform their economies while they're drowning in disasters and debt," he wrote.

    According to recent reports, the climate activist stressed that the reason this COP failed wasn't a lack of solutions. It was due to "a lack of money and a lack of will from those who caused this crisis," he mentioned.

    Carbon capture technology works, but its real-world capabilities are nowhere near to moving the needle on climate change. So what's the hold-up?

    Attacks on climate science and disinformation seem to be delaying key decisions as the UN climate talks draw to a close in Antalya.

    Leaders from Africa, one of the continents worst hit by climate change, have spent years lobbying for hundreds of billions of dollars to help adapt to the rising impacts of global warming.

    The rest of the world relies on African nations for their abundant natural resources, many of them used in clean energy production.

    Yet at COP31, wealthy nations have so far failed to commit to the financing needed to help developing nations make a just transition.

    Read our report from DW's Kathy Wood.

    The head of Peru's delegation at COP31, Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, warned that the UN climate summit was unlikely to end with a concrete deal on climate financing or cutting fossil fuel use.

    Garrido Sanchez lamented that the outcome "would be very limited.".

    He reiterated how "geopolitical divisions" were stopping any final deal from mentioning reducing reliance on oil, gas and coal.

    The Peruvian delegate singled out major oil producers, such as Gulf Arab states and Russia, as showing significant opposition.

    He noted that while Latin American neighbor Panama had also signaled objection to including the term fossil fuels in the final text, Peru was "not so radical" and is keen to attract investment to "ensure our energy security" through renewables.

    China has backed a initiative proposed by COP host Turkey to raise global electricity demand to 35% by 2035 — up from the current 20%.

    Industry observers note that in a joint statement with Australia, which is leading negotiations between almost 200 nations at the COP31 summit in Turkey, Beijing stated it welcomes "growing international ambition and cooperation ... to increase electricity's share of global final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035 on a voluntary basis.".

    The statement goes on to highlight the benefits the transition can bring for the economy, jobs, energy security, public health and households.

    The two partners also "acknowledge the importance of inclusive climate action that ensures no one is left behind," the text continued.

    Dozens of countries, including EU states, Japan, South Korea and Canada, have so far signaled support for the voluntary goal, which aims to boost clean energy use.

    Yet, environmental groups have warned that the draft text doesn't stipulate the use of solar, wind and other renewable energy sources, which could allow power plants using natural gas and coal to be included.

    It has been revealed that earlier this week at the DealBook conference in Newly introduced York, Elon Musk, beamed in from a trip to China with President Donald Trump, was asked about the ouster of his longtime friend, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Musk compared it to kicking Michael Jordan off the Chicago Bulls’ roster during his historic run. Of Nvidia’s employees, he noted, “They love [Huang]. They love him.”.

    It has been revealed that well, maybe not all of them. Thousands of employees have signed a letter asking for Huang’s return, but others tell The Fresh York Times he ruled through praise and fear, as well as by humiliating people.

    According to the Times, Huang told subordinates that Nvidia’s wealth meant it wasn’t possible to motivate employees with money, so humiliation was the only lever left. He reportedly told one executive his mother should have aborted him and told another employee he would rip his arms off and beat him to death with them.

    Naturally, over a 33-year career, regrettable things may have been said, but the Times found a long paper trail that suggests the incidents weren’t isolated. In 2005, for example, Michael Winston, a former HR chief, threatened to sue and called Huang’s conduct the most abusive he’d seen. Nvidia paid him more than $1 million. Huang’s spokesman calls the allegations fabrications.

    #70246. Industry News: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA indicates nearby phones will be jammed too.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1282 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA indicates nearby phones will be jammed too.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1282 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons.
    • Wireless industry lobby group CTIA remarked a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls.
    • It has been revealed that the pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons.

    Wireless industry lobby group CTIA remarked a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing:.

    It has been revealed that the pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts.

    CTIA noted the pilot test reveals “that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications.”.

    In a recent development, the FCC approved the jamming order at its meeting yesterday. “Today, we are finally authorizing state and local prisons and jails to use targeted jamming against contraband cell phones for the first time,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr remarked. “The technology has advanced to the point where it can be focused with geographic precision. No facility will be required to do it.”.

    The Communications Act prohibits willful or malicious interference with licensed or authorized radio communications, and the FCC has previously interpreted this to prohibit non-federal entities from using jamming technology on contraband devices at prisons. Yesterday’s vote provides an exception for state and local correctional facilities. The FCC indicates its jammer prohibitions do not apply to federal agencies because the federal government’s use of spectrum is not regulated by the agency.

    Carr said that “contraband cell phones continue to pour into prisons by the thousands each year,” with “estimates indicat[ing] that as many as 500,000 inmates nationwide have regular access to these devices.” He said the phones have been used to plan scams, drug trafficking, and violent attacks.

    “In Georgia, an incarcerated gang leader directed a drive-by shooting that killed two 13-year-old boys at a birthday party,” Carr said, referring to a 2024 shooting.

    Carr defended the plan against criticism that it will block legitimate communications outside the prisons, saying it includes safeguards to prevent that.

    “Those that want to use the technology will apply to the FCC, explain how they plan to deploy it, and show through testing that it stays inside the designated area and doesn’t interfere with lawful communications outside the prison walls,” Carr stated. “Communities nearby will receive notice before operations start. We’re also seeking comment on next steps, including ways to close remaining loopholes on other frequencies and the possibility of quiet zones around correctional facilities.”.

    Freedom of the Press Foundation Chief of Advocacy Seth Stern remarked the FCC should have considered the benefits of contraband phones being used to document abuses inside prisons.

    According to recent reports, “Prisons are the most secretive government institutions in the country and people wishing to expose abuses and inhumane conditions from the inside often do not have many options,” Stern wrote in a letter to FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez’s office, which was included on the FCC docket. “Last year’s Oscar-nominated film, The Alabama Solution, used footage incarcerated people captured with contraband cell phones to show Americans some of the awful things that go on in state prisons that they’d have no other way of seeing. The same footage bolstered an ongoing DOJ investigation into Alabama prisons and was crucial evidence in a civil lawsuit by Steven Davis, who was brutally killed by prison guards, that eventually settled.”.

    Jamming contraband cellphones was supported by prison phone companies ViaPath (aka Global Tel*Link) and NCIC Correctional Services, the National District Attorneys Association, the Correctional Leaders Association, and National Association of Police Organizations.

    “Inmates have used these phones to coordinate attacks against correctional officers and their families, as well as inmate violence, strikes, disturbances, and full-scale riots,” the National Association of Police Organizations said. “They also use contraband phones to organize deliveries of illegal drugs and weapons into correctional facilities. These dangers underscore the need to authorize indoor jamming in state and local correctional facilities.”.

    Gomez, the only Democrat on the three-member commission, said she’s concerned about potential unintended consequences, but voted with Republicans to allow jamming after safeguards were added to the order.

    “For the last 90 years, the Federal Communications Commission has prohibited jamming by non-federal actors and even prohibited jamming equipment to be introduced into the American market,” Gomez stated. “That is because jamming devices are specifically designed to interfere with communications devices in order to render them un-usable.”.

    Gomez stated that “jamming can prevent devices from completing 911 and emergency calls as well as interfere with communications networks used by fire, police, Emergency Medical Services, and other public safety entities.” She also said making jamming equipment available in the American market could lead to “unauthorized sale of this hazardous equipment,” and that “the accessibility of jamming equipment can itself motivate criminal enterprise.” Criminals have used “Wi-Fi jammers to disrupt security systems, security cameras, and cellphones to conduct robberies at homes and at stores,” she said.

    Gomez said she’s glad the final order includes safeguards “to ensure that jamming is contained to this unique use, to permit jamming by a very limited category of authorized actors, and to take as much care as possible to prevent jamming and jamming equipment from becoming a hazard to safety.”.

    According to recent reports, gomez partially dissented because she is worried the FCC will let correctional facilities and prison phone companies charge higher prices for inmate calling services that connect inmates with family members. Under US law, the FCC sets limits on those prices and considers prisons’ and jails’ safety and security costs when deciding how much money they can charge, she said.

    Gomez said, “While correctional facilities should have safety and security services like jamming to prevent criminal activity, it is not the responsibility of the families of incarcerated people to pay for the costs of these measures… Jamming is specifically designed to block communications and is certainly not necessary to provide phone and video calls for incarcerated individuals. We should have made this clear in today’s order. Because we failed to do so, I dissent in part.”.

    The FCC order could be challenged in court. The CTIA has argued that the FCC “has no authority to allow jamming” under the Communications Act, which directs the FCC to prevent interference.

    According to recent reports, AT&T stated the FCC’s legal justification “is premised on a fundamental factual error: the assumption that jammers will only block ‘unauthorized’ communications without impacting lawful uses. There is no way to jam some communications on a spectrum band but not others. That is because radio jammers ‘block all wireless communications on affected spectrum bands,’ and, as the FCC has noted in the past, ‘cannot differentiate between contraband devices and legitimate devices.’”.

    Sources indicate that AT&T noted that “there is simply no way to limit the reach of jammers to the confines of a given facility. Jammers have been shown to cause interference outside the facilities in which they operate, greatly increasing the risk that someone living or traveling nearby will be impacted.”.

    iPad Air vs. iPad Pro: The features you're actually paying $450 extra for

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (993 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The iPad Pro is Apple's best tablet, but not everyone needs its power.
    • When choosing your next iPad, it's not a difficult decision if you know the base model works for your needs, or if you want a small tablet.
    • The iPad Air starts at $749 for the 11-inch model with 128GB of storage and an M4 processor, while the 11-inch M5 256GB base iPad Pro costs $1,199.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The iPad Pro is Apple's best tablet, but not everyone needs its power.

    When choosing your next iPad, it's not a difficult decision if you know the base model works for your needs, or if you want a small tablet. But it's trickier to decide between the iPad Air and iPad Pro if you're using an iPad for work or creative pursuits. Is saving $450 and opting for the still-capable iPad Air something you'll regret in the future?

    The iPad Air starts at $749 for the 11-inch model with 128GB of storage and an M4 processor, while the 11-inch M5 256GB base iPad Pro costs $1,199. Both devices offer 13-inch variants if you want a larger screen. Those prices might seem higher than you remember, due to the ongoing RAM crisis that's been spiking consumer tech prices. Apple hasn't been immune to its effects, and has passed those costs onto would-be iPad customers.

    It has been revealed that while the iPad Pro packs plenty of improvements, its strongest selling point is what meets your eyes right away: the display. It also relies on a faster processor that makes a meaningful difference in intensive apps. Picking between it and the Air comes down to how you initiative to take advantage of the Pro's advanced spec sheet.

    It has been revealed that the iPad Air's laminated IPS LED display is great, with solid color accuracy, P3 wide color gamut support and a pixel density of 264 ppi that makes text crisp and clear to read. The iPad Pro also has a pixel density of 264 ppi, but that's where the similarities end.

    Industry observers note that at 1,000 nits and up to 1,600 nits with HDR, the Pro's brighter tandem OLED display is miles ahead of the Air's 500-nit display. It relies on two OLED panels stacked on each other to boost brightness and color accuracy. With a contrast ratio of 2,000,000:1, it has incredibly deep blacks, which are appreciated for video creation and consumption alike.

    Industry observers note that its 120Hz ProMotion display also feels smoother as you work through app menus, play games or simply scroll through the interface. To conserve battery, it can drop down to 10Hz while displaying images or other static content like a webpage. To reduce reflections and hide smudges, Apple also offers a nano-texture glass option at an additional cost for the top-tier Pro models.

    The latest iPad Air debuted in March 2026 and relies on Apple's M4 chip, while the Pro stepped up to an M5 in October 2025. To put that in context, the iPad Pro lineup used M4 back in 2024. The M4 processor is more than enough for most tasks, including gaming and video editing. It can handle rendering, media editing and on-device AI tools with no problem.

    However, we found that the M5 in the iPad Pro was twice as fast when it came to running local AI models for advanced image generation tools. It offers 45 percent higher graphics performance and 15 percent faster multithreaded performance over the M4 processor.

    With the M5 chip, you'll shave off a couple of seconds across intensive tasks. Admittedly, these are niche use cases, but if you want the best hardware Apple offers, paying more for the Pro model saves you time across the experience. The uptick in performance also lets the iPad Pro drive external displays at 120Hz, while the Air is restricted to 60Hz.

    It has been revealed that while the camera is seldom on the priority list when considering an iPad, the iPad Pro relies on some nifty tech uncommon among tablets. A Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensor next to the Pro models' rear camera helps with better autofocus and AR scanning.

    According to recent reports, through third-party apps like Polycam, it can make floor maps of your home and develop 3D renders. Apple's Measure app lets the iPad Pro accurately measure item heights and the distance between objects, making it a great assistant when you're getting new furniture or rearranging the house. While the iPad Air also has the Measure app, it lacks this sensor that enhances its accuracy.

    According to recent reports, on the front, the Pro supports Face ID, letting you unlock your tablet without a password, while the iPad Air still relies on a fingerprint sensor for Touch ID. The advanced TrueDepth camera array also grants the ability to develop a spatial render of your face for Animoji and Memoji, or Portrait Mode selfies with background blur adjustments.

    According to recent reports, the iPad Pro comes with twice the base storage (128GB vs. 256GB), plus quad speakers compared to the Air's stereo speaker setup. It also supports fast charging with a 60W power adapter (not included), while its Thunderbolt 3 / USB 4 USB-C port can transfer large files faster and drive external monitors at 120Hz. The Pros used to have more RAM than the Air models, but the M4 Air matches them with 12GB of unified memory.

    It has been revealed that the iPad Pro keeps these advantages in a body that's only 5.3mm (0.21 inches) deep, slimmer than the already impressive 6.1mm (0.24 inches) of the iPad Air. They offer the same 10 hours of battery life for web browsing and video streaming. Individually, these features may not mean much outside of specific purposes. But together, they can make a compelling argument for the cost.

    Despite these advantages, there's not enough here for a casual user that would justify spending $450 more for the iPad Pro. At $749, the iPad Air strikes the right balance of performance and features despite Apple's price hike this year from its prior price of $599. If you aren't going to take advantage of the iPad Pro's extra horsepower for video and photo editing, or by making the iPad your primary work device, your needs will be served just as well by the more affordable iPad Air.

    • Karen Scarborough (left) and Anne Lindboe got to work with a two-handled saw.
    • This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.
    • The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Karen Scarborough (left) and Anne Lindboe got to work with a two-handled saw.

    This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.

    The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old. It was felled on Friday by the Lord Mayor of Westminster, Karen Scarborough, and the Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe.

    Norway has sent a tree to the capital every year since 1947 as a thank you for Britain's support during World War Two, when King Haakon VII and the Norwegian government lived in exile in London.

    Its lights will be switched on by the two mayors at a ceremony in the square on Thursday, 3 December.

    Scarborough remarked: "It's my greatest honour to take part in this wonderful tradition for both the cities of Oslo and London.

    "This tree is a powerful symbol of friendship and peace, reminding us to be there for one another during the festive period.".

    The 21m tree has been nicknamed Jolly Cheery.

    Scarborough thanked "the people of Oslo and Norway for this truly fabulous gift" and added: "With the care and dedication of the team, I'm sure it will look magnificent on Trafalgar Square.".

    Lindboe said: "Oslo has been sending a Christmas tree to London for almost eight decades, and every year we send a tree across the North Sea with the same message: we have not forgotten.

    "The tradition has a powerful history, and its message remains just as relevant today.

    "I hope Jolly Cheery spreads warmth and Christmas cheer to everyone who passes by, and reminds us how much it means to be there for one another, especially in difficult times.".

    Count the rings: Anne Lindboe (left) and Karen Scarborough (right) with a slice of the 75-year-old trunk.

    For the second year running, the tree was chosen with the help of a social media poll.

    Organisers remarked it would travel by road in Norway and England using only electric and biodiesel vehicles, cutting the journey's carbon footprint by 80%. It will cross the North Sea on a regular cargo ship from the port of Brevik.

    Once in London, it will be decorated in the traditional Norwegian style, with 25m strings of festoon lighting fitted with energy-efficient bulbs.

    #70242. ‘Six, seven, maybe more preventable deaths’: Queensland’s LNP faces reckoning over broken health system

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (996 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theguardian ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘Six, seven, maybe more preventable deaths’: Queensland’s LNP faces reckoning over broken health system

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A government in office for more than two years is finally forced to take responsibility and seemingly no longer able to blame its Labor predecessors.
    • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.
    • At the beginning of another Queensland parliamentary sitting week, anonymous sources were out in force, this time background briefing against the state’s Labor leader, Steven Miles.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A government in office for more than two years is finally forced to take responsibility and seemingly no longer able to blame its Labor predecessors.

    Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

    At the beginning of another Queensland parliamentary sitting week, anonymous sources were out in force, this time background briefing against the state’s Labor leader, Steven Miles.

    It has been revealed that it is no great revelation to observers of Queensland politics that Miles, still seemingly bruised from his election loss two years ago, has struggled to find his feet as opposition leader. Many wondered why he wanted to stay on after the party’s drubbing in 2024. Some of Labor’s factional whisperers were telling anyone who would listen that the former premier’s leadership would come to an end in the weeks before Christmas.

    However, the week in parliament has ended with a revitalised opposition and a wounded LNP government. A government that has for so long seemed untouchable. A government that has now been left battling the perception that it is overseeing a broken health system.

    And a government – now in office for more than two years – finally forced to take responsibility for systems it had promised to repair; seemingly no longer able to legitimately blame the former Labor government for the litany of mistakes that led to the deaths of seven people in the care of Queensland’s health system.

    By the end of the week, parliament heard six people had died waiting for an ambulance in the last three weeks. One man had waited seven hours, another three. All were triaged as urgently in need of attention.

    Another man had taken his own life in the emergency department of the Prince Charles hospital after self-admitting for mental health treatment. It took staff three hours to find him.

    The health minister, Tim Nicholls, is a professional, a 20-year veteran, with the bearing of a well-paid barrister, who led the LNP to an election in 2017.

    But he struggled to cope with the parliamentary barrage.

    In response to a question from Labor’s Joe Kelly, a former nurse, about how many ambulances had been ramped on 3 November, the night a man died while waiting for one in Townsville, Nicholls first criticised the question’s “pettiness”.

    “What next? Are they going to ask me what the level of fuel was in the back of the ambulances?” he responded.

    “There was no ramping overnight at the Townsville University hospital that night,” he finished.

    “I am very pleased to be able to correct the record for the purposes of the house,” he stated, two questions later.

    According to recent reports, “There were at that time four ambulances, as I understand it, on the ramp waiting to off-load. That was the situation there.”.

    Nicholls threw the blame at the federal government, at the former Labor state government and its “decade of decline”, a phrase repeated endlessly by government MPs, at overwhelmed hospitals full of “forgotten Australians”, a term used to refer to retirees warehoused in public hospitals for lack of a federally funded retirement home to put them in.

    Endlessly, Labor hounded him: would he meet the families of the dead?

    The answer was not quite no, but never yes either.

    For a government built on a small-target strategy based on responding to the grief of victims of crime – predicated on the fact that any indecisive response to a tragedy would be an inherently unconvincing one – this was a completely different emotional battle.

    By Wednesday, Nicholls was attending an emergency meeting with the premier, David Crisafulli, the health department director general, David Rosengren, and the ambulance service commissioner, Craig Emery.

    The next day, after another bruising question time, he called a press conference.

    Bearing his well-worn years-old folder labelled “LABOR’S HOSPITAL FAILURES”, he insisted that he was taking responsibility – for making sure his subordinates were doing their jobs.

    “I think people would expect that, as the minister, I hold the DG and the commissioner responsible for the services that they deliver, and I seek answers to questions,” he remarked.

    “So I sought advice from the commissioner about the steps that they were taking, what was being done to address the need, what was the root cause of the problem.”.

    Nicholls mentioned the community could have confidence in the triple-zero system and paramedics, promising to reinvest whatever it was he needed to, on advice from his department.

    “Like all Queenslanders, I do have questions regarding the delivery of services because one death that’s unexpected in the community is one too many,” he stated.

    “Every available vehicle is on the road. But the issue is there are simply not enough beds.”.

    After 10 minutes, with many more questions unasked, he abruptly walked off, looking more like a traditional Queensland health minister than any in the LNP cabinet have this term.

    Then Miles stepped up to the microphone. After days of leadership speculation in newspapers – which has been deliberately and mischievously fanned by the government – the former health minister was on much more solid ground.

    “I have never before seen so many preventable deaths of Queenslanders left waiting hours for an ambulance to arrive, only to die before it does,” Miles said.

    “Six, seven, maybe more preventable deaths.

    Recent findings suggest that “It is only getting worse and worse. The worst that it’s ever been.”.

    Miles retains significant goodwill from most Labor MPs, but the polls have become hard for most to ignore. Some think he’s simply failed to land enough punches. Others that he hasn’t thrown nearly enough.

    It remains to be seen whether Miles’s decision to come out swinging was the act of an opposition leader with nothing to lose, deciding to fight at five minutes to midnight in his political career.

    One thing is certain. After two years in which the opposition has rarely felt relevant, this week Queensland politics finally felt like a fair fight.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • From notetakers to webcams that follow your movements, here are six AI-powered gadgets worth checking out if you want to upgrade your workspace.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tech companies are racing to figure out how AI can make everyday work a little easier.

    From notetakers to webcams that follow your movements, here are six AI-powered gadgets worth checking out if you want to upgrade your workspace.

    If you’re constantly scribbling notes during meetings, the Flowtica Scribe could save you from having to type everything up afterward.

    The AI-powered pen combines traditional handwriting with audio recording. You can use its built-in gel pen to take notes, tap the side to highlight important points, and press the end of the pen to start recording audio. Once the meeting is over, its AI can transcribe the conversation, summarize key takeaways, and create a to-do list based on what was discussed.

    You can even ask the AI questions about the meeting to find specific information without having to go through the entire recording.

    The Scribe comes with a built-in microphone and 32GB of onboard storage. It can also identify up to 15 different speakers and supports 92 languages.

    Anker’s AI-powered recording pin, Soundcore Work, is designed to capture conversations, meetings, and quick voice memos without taking up much space on your desk.

    Priced at $159 (currently reduced to $99 in the Amazon Black Friday sale), the coin-sized device comes with a puck-shaped charging case and can record for up to eight hours on a single charge, extending to 32 hours when used with its case. Anker also claims a recording range of up to 5 meters, making it useful for capturing conversations around a meeting table.

    Sources indicate that the companion app handles transcription and uses AI to turn recordings into more organized notes and summaries. Customers also get 300 minutes of free audio transcription each month.

    If you need more recording capacity or access to additional AI features, Anker offers optional subscription prepares, including Pro ($99 per year) and Unlimited ($239 per year).

    Recent findings suggest that logitech’s MX Keypad brings AI shortcuts directly to your desk, with dedicated buttons that let you launch your preferred AI assistant or trigger specific productivity tools with a single press. If you frequently switch between different apps and AI assistants, having these shortcuts within reach could make your workday easier.

    The keypad can be configured to work with tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code, along with a range of popular productivity and creative apps, such as OpenAI Codex, Microsoft Teams, PowerPoint, Excel, Notion, Slack, Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Zoom, and Figma.

    Amazon’s Kindle Scribe Colorsoft brings color to the company’s digital notetaking lineup and offers some neat AI features designed to clean up your messy notes.

    Starting at $479, the device is aimed at people who regularly work with digital documents, including students, researchers, and professionals who prefer annotating files rather than printing them out. It lets you highlight notable passages, mark up documents, organize handwritten notes, and sketch out ideas.

    Notably, the Scribe Colorsoft incorporates AI-powered tools to clean up messy handwriting, straighten highlighting and underlining, summarize notes, and help turn scattered thoughts into more organized information. Its search feature can look across your saved notes to find specific details and help identify connections between different entries.

    If you’re tired of adjusting your webcam during video calls, Insta360’s Link 2 Pro aims to take care of that for you.

    According to recent reports, priced at $249 (discounted to $199 for Black Friday), this AI-powered webcam combines 4K video capture with intelligent tracking and automatic framing. Its smart video tracker can follow your movements and adjust the camera’s position to keep you in view, even when you move around your workspace, which is particularly useful for people who regularly give presentations, teach online, or switch between sitting at their desk and standing during video calls.

    The camera also offers group tracking, which can come in handy during team meetings or presentations involving multiple people. AI-powered noise cancellation is another useful addition, helping reduce distracting background sounds during calls.

    In a recent development, your desk could probably use a little intelligence, too. Autonomous Desk Pro is an adjustable standing desk designed to encourage healthier habits throughout the workday.

    Beyond switching between sitting and standing positions, the AI-powered desk uses built-in sensors to monitor your activity and remind you when it’s time to move, stretch, or change positions. It can track how much time you spend sitting versus standing, giving you a better idea of your daily work habits.

    The AI features go a step further by allowing you to ask questions about your activity. For example, you can check how long you’ve been sitting, compare your activity with the previous day, or get information about the room’s CO2 levels to help determine whether it’s time to open a window.

    China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (998 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’.
    • China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.
    • The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it stated was the protection of diplomatic immunity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’.

    China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.

    The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it stated was the protection of diplomatic immunity.

    The statement affirmed that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought”, but stopped short of suggesting the beginnings of a framework for denuclearisation.

    The meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump has dominated the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit this week, with China, the host, promising it would be “groundbreaking”.

    According to recent reports, “We are really making history,” Trump told Xi and Putin at the start of the meeting. “No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement.”.

    Putin told a press conference later that the three men had had a “free discussion” and now had a “mutual understanding”.

    In a recent development, some had hopes that the talks, which lasted about one hour and 20 minutes, could be used to discuss reductions in arms between the world’s three largest nuclear powers. Beijing has previously rebuffed Trump’s advances to join such talks, pointing to the larger US and Russian stockpiles. On Thursday, though, Xi called for nuclear weapons to “be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of [them]”.

    The language of the declaration around nuclear war is the same as that previously issued by the five permanent members of the UN security council, which includes France and the UK.

    “The real test will be whether the three countries follow through on their stated commitment to discuss nuclear risk reduction and preventing nuclear proliferation,” said Patricia Kim, an expert on Chinese foreign policy at the Brookings Institution, a US thinktank. Even the suggestion that China would engage was significant, said Yun Sun, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center.

    It has been revealed that analysts had noted that the meeting’s primary significance was in its optics. “Overall, very little of substance seems to have been accomplished … This summit appears to have been all about the symbolism and prestige value,” said Prof William Hurst, from the University of Cambridge’s Centre for Geopolitics. Putin pushed back at the suggestion the summit had just been a photo-op. “It is a serious collaborative work,” he said.

    In the declaration, the men “committed themselves to maintaining strategic stability and international security”.

    First among their concerns was “promoting UN reform so that it may respond more effectively to global challenges”. Sun mentioned this was a favourite topic of China’s and showed that Beijing was “flexing its diplomatic muscles”. She said: “It is able to set the agenda and the deliverables according to its priorities … and make other great powers accept them.”.

    The declaration also agreed that “the international criminal court [ICC] and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction”. Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant and so the clause added to the perception that he has done well from the summit. Since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, the Russian president has been treated as an international pariah by Kyiv’s allies and he has not been to an Apec summit in years.

    Industry observers note that hurst noted: “This was no Yalta moment, but it was certainly a solid public demonstration of Russia’s (and Putin’s) continuing relevance and power. It’s yet another example of Putin playing a poor hand to maximum effect.”.

    Xi, his status as a global power broker now assured, began the morning by addressing Apec leaders, reiterating the themes of trade openness and innovation he has emphasised throughout the summit. However, Apec affairs appeared to take a back seat for most of the day, with business dominating the discussions. For all the camaraderie on display, relations are complex. Russia is under US sanctions over the Ukraine war, while China and the US spent much of the last year engaged in an escalating tit-for-tat trade war before Trump and Xi called a truce.

    Trump and Putin earlier held a separate meeting – their first since August 2025 – where the US president called his Russian counterpart his “friend”.

    Recent findings suggest that european allies meeting in Berlin to show their support for Ukraine expressed indignation at the cosy optics. “Mr Putin is not our friend and ⁠will never be,” the Polish prime minister, Donald Tusk, mentioned in a rejoinder to Trump. The Danish prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, said she found it “very incomprehensible” that a US ​president would want to sit down with Putin.

    The peace declaration in Shenzhen said the three countries planned “to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations”. That was crucial, said Shan Guo from Hutong Research, a Shanghai-based advisory firm, but “now let’s see if the US will lift sanctions”.

    It has been revealed that trump and Xi then held their third bilateral of this year. Xi said the US-China relationship was “generally stable and positive”, according to state media. But he cautioned Washington over Taiwan, saying the US “must keep doing the right thing to avoid major setbacks in US-China relations”.

    Another watched-for topic lacking detailed findings was that of AI. Xi said the two countries should “enhance communication and coordination to guard against security risks … and ensure that AI remains under human control at all times”.

    Ultimately, the lack of breakthroughs might suit China, which has no appetite to move beyond the role of convener, remarked Kim. “Beijing has little interest in taking on the diplomatic risks of brokering an actual peace agreement in Ukraine or resolving the conflict with Iran. That would entangle China in conflicts it would rather avoid,” she said.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, the notorious Rikers Island jail complex earned a variety of nicknames over the years.
    • Latest York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new strategy from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.
    • Mamdani on Friday unveiled a plan to close the Rikers Island complex by 2032, to build four fresh jails and drastically reduce the city's detainee population.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, the notorious Rikers Island jail complex earned a variety of nicknames over the years.

    Latest York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new strategy from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.

    Mamdani on Friday unveiled a plan to close the Rikers Island complex by 2032, to build four fresh jails and drastically reduce the city's detainee population.

    Plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it by this year. But plans have been delayed over the years in part due to the logistical difficulties over where to place inmates.

    Dana Kaplan - who Mamdani appointed as the city's "Close Rikers Czar" told the BBC News channel on Friday that his latest proposal is not just about getting rid of a decrepit facility.

    It is also a "generational opportunity" to "build a different type of detention system" and figure out how to detain people more appropriately, she noted.

    Recent findings suggest that the Rikers Island jail complex is perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, and has earned a variety of nicknames over the years because of its dilapidated conditions, including Gladiator School and Torture Island. The jail has housed a number of high-profile inmates awaiting trial, including Tupac Shakur, DMX and Harvey Weinstein.

    It has been revealed that it houses more than 6,500 inmates at a given time. Mamdani hopes to reduce that number to 4,100 - a goal that has been met with skepticism by the Latest York City correction officers' union.

    "[B]uilding a new system that puts an arbitrary cap on the City's available jail beds is ill-conceived, irresponsible and jeopardizes the safety of all New Yorkers, including our Officers," NYC Correction Officers' Benevolent Association said in a statement. "The City cannot keep the jail population at around 4,100 without irresponsibly releasing individuals who committed violent felony charges.".

    "It's actually possible to have fewer people in jail in Latest York City - and that is what we should be planning for," she said.

    The jail complex has long faced backlash over staffing shortages, crumbling conditions and inmate deaths in the facility, including nine this year. Legislation required the jail to be shuttered by 2027, but Mamdani blamed lags under former Mayor Eric Adams' administration as well as the Covid pandemic for the delays.

    Last year, under Adams, a federal judge removed Rikers from the city's control, appointing an independent outside official to make decisions concerning the facility.

    In an 88-page report released on Friday, Mamdani said Rikers was a product of "deteriorating infrastructure" and that officials had a "moral imperative" to close it.

    Latest York City Council must approve the updated timeline, with members, including the city's speaker, indicating they support the strategy.

    Mamdani's office noted the city would open up four fresh jails - one in Brooklyn by 2029, two in the Bronx and Queens by 2031 and one in Manhattan by 2032.

    The mayor's office argues the latest, smaller facilities will provide inmates "access to daylight, fresh air and clean space" leading to better outcomes for detainees. The facilities will be easier for families to access as well, as travel to the remote Rikers can take hours.

    Mamdani stated his administration would work to reduce the number of people being held in jail across New York City, including by offering alternative programmes to detention for some awaiting trial, by making it easier for families to post bail online and by trying to speed up the pretrial legal process.

    He also wants to open up hundreds of beds in therapeutic housing units for prisoners with serious mental health issues.

    Kaplan stated Mamdani's administration had already opened 100 therapeutic beds at Bellevue Hospital in Manhattan, moving 100 people off of Rikers Island.

    The proposal involves a large investments: $146m (Â£111m) for mental health and substance use treatment and vocational and education programming inside and outside the jails.

    #70234. Why does your phone say no service even with a SIM card?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (731 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    Why does your phone say no service even with a SIM card?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (731 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If your calls and texts aren't going through, try these recommendations.
    • Sources indicate that the modern electronic device has made a lot of strides in ensuring that it lets you know when something has gone awry.
    • In a recent development, on your phone, you may notice one of these alerts in the form of a notification that says, "No SIM card installed." This can be alarming, as it's possible that you may not know what a SIM card even does.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If your calls and texts aren't going through, try these recommendations.

    Sources indicate that the modern electronic device has made a lot of strides in ensuring that it lets you know when something has gone awry. Things like computers, game consoles and tablets will often find a way to alert you to an issue, which makes it easier to troubleshoot any potential problems that may arise.

    In a recent development, on your phone, you may notice one of these alerts in the form of a notification that says, "No SIM card installed." This can be alarming, as it's possible that you may not know what a SIM card even does. Or if you do know what the SIM card does, it can lead to some worrying conclusions as you try to troubleshoot it.

    Fixing a SIM card error is a task that requires some diagnostic detective work, or if you're extra unlucky, some actual physical work. Thankfully, there are a lot of tools, both in your phone's settings and in the real world, that can assist with a potential fix.

    When a SIM card error leaves you without service, the phone will still work and power on; it will just be without its main features. The only thing that needs to be done is to take it out and put it right back in. This is usually caused by dropping the phone or ithe card not being properly seated when it was serviced for you, but you can use a SIM ejector tool to take it out. If you don't have one, something as simple as a paper clip or safety pin will usually do the trick.

    It's always worth finding out if it's something as simple as a carrier outage, which is entirely possible. If you have access to another device on a different carrier and it can connect to the internet or make a phone call, that could indicate a network outage specific to your carrier. Asking a local friend or family member using the same service whether their phone is working properly can confirm a carrier outage or eliminate it as a possibility.

    It has been revealed that your phone may be using an eSIM card, which replaces the physical card with a digital SIM. These are great, but they tend to have unique complications with international travel. If you're using an eSIM card, the way you access settings on an iPhone is slightly different from Android. On an iPhone, eSIM cards are located in Cellular or Mobile Data in the Settings menu, while Android stores them in a setting called SIM Manager. By turning on data roaming, you may fix any sort of problems you're having.

    A SIM card or "no service" error can sometimes be something at a software level as opposed to something being wrong with the card. One of the more common fixes is simply toggling airplane mode on and off. Airplane mode can be found by swiping down from the top of your phone and tapping the airplane button.

    You may also be able to do a quick network reset, which sounds bad but has zero effect on your personal files. Doing a network reset on an iPhone is largely similar to the process on Android. It should be noted, however, that the iPhone's network reset is in the Transfer or Reset section of Settings, while Android stores it in Reset Options, also in Settings. You will need to sign back into your Wi-Fi, however, along with some other connections.

    Recent findings suggest that we all get busy in life, and if you haven't paid your bill, then your SIM card will simply stop connecting to your carrier's network. It may seem like a simple thing, but sometimes the simple solutions are blindingly obvious. If you pay your bill online, check your account to see if you've missed a payment or if your service hasn't been suspended for some other reason.

    Getting no service on your phone may not even have anything to do with a bad SIM card or an inactive account. You may just be in a place with limited to no service available, or a cellphone tower may be blocked by something. Move around and look for someplace that you actually can connect, as the error may be a result of poor service in that area.

    #70232. NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2339 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2339 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SpaceX’s successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA’s path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-important, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year.
    • For SpaceX’s purposes, Saturday’s mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships.
    • Recent findings suggest that early next year, SpaceX prepares to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SpaceX’s successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA’s path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-important, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year.

    For SpaceX’s purposes, Saturday’s mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships. That should expedite SpaceX’s deployment of its newest generation of Starlink Internet satellites. NASA, meanwhile, believes a higher launch cadence will lead to faster learning as SpaceX develops a deep space version of Starship to ferry astronaut crews to the surface of the Moon.

    Recent findings suggest that early next year, SpaceX prepares to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. A second Starship factory is also under construction at Kennedy, joining SpaceX’s existing SpaceX production line at Starbase, Texas. With two launch sites, SpaceX will have the pieces in place to take the next leap with Starship.

    It has been revealed that the Starship refueling demonstration has slipped two years since late 2024, effectively a day-for-day delay as SpaceX ironed out technical problems with the vehicle. SpaceX may have turned a corner with Saturday’s first-ever catch of Starship at the launch tower.

    Other Starship lander tests are coming next year. The first will be NASA’s Artemis III mission, followed by an uncrewed Starship landing demonstration on the Moon. The former requires no orbital refueling, and the latter will need heaps of it.

    Sources indicate that ars recently spoke with Steve Creech, the program manager for NASA’s Human Landing System. In this role, Creech oversees NASA’s contracts with SpaceX and Blue Origin to develop crew-rated lunar landers for Artemis.

    Sources indicate that for Artemis III, NASA will launch a four-person crew to low-Earth orbit on a Space Launch System rocket and an Orion spacecraft. Orion will first dock with Blue Origin’s Blue Moon lander for two days of tests, following its launch on a Latest Glenn rocket. The astronauts will open hatches and enter Blue Moon’s pressurized crew cabin to test the vehicle’s environmental control and life support systems.

    According to recent reports, then, the astronauts will return to Orion and undock from Blue Moon to set up for a rendezvous and docking with SpaceX’s Starship in a slightly lower orbit, keeping it below most of SpaceX’s Starlink constellation. Orion will stay attached to Starship for just two hours, and the astronauts won’t enter the SpaceX vehicle.

    According to recent reports, NASA changed the proposal for the Artemis III mission earlier this year, rerouting the flight plan from a lunar mission to a low-Earth orbit mission. This means the Artemis program’s first crewed lunar landing will be on Artemis IV, targeted to launch before the end of 2028.

    In a recent development, so, why is Artemis III seemingly testing so much more with Blue Origin than with Starship? Creech told Ars that a significant reason is to maintain SpaceX’s focus on orbital refueling. Blue Origin no longer requires in-space refueling for Artemis landing missions. Also, SpaceX has extensive experience with life support systems with its Dragon crewed spacecraft. Blue Origin has comparatively little.

    It has been revealed that “The bigger challenges for [SpaceX] were the prop transfer and getting to the uncrewed landing demo,” Creech stated. “The thing that we’re going to learn more with Starship is, when we dock with Orion, they will have control of the attitude, control of the stack. That integrated stack control will be on the Starship side. So, with that huge of a vehicle, I think we’re going to learn more on that.

    “With Blue, we’re going to have Orion control the stack for this mission,” Creech said. “When we get to a later mission, the Blue lander with fully loaded prop will have to control the stack. But with Blue, trying to mitigate risk, we’re going to have Orion do that.”.

    According to recent reports, artemis III will be Blue Origin’s first time flying a crew cabin for orbital spaceflight. Blue Origin has experience with suborbital space tourism, but those flights were brief and didn’t require the level of advanced life support necessary for longer durations. Blue Origin and NASA will emphasize those test objectives on Artemis III.

    Recent findings suggest that “I think SpaceX’s part was really, we need to focus on the docking,” Creech noted. “If we added a crew cabin, that would slow us down on the other things and not add to what we’re already doing.”.

    The Starship on Artemis III will have a full complement of Raptor engines and a docking port on its nose. Blue Moon will not have any main engines when it links up with Orion on Artemis III, only a set of smaller thrusters for pointing control and minor maneuvers.

    Sources indicate that “With Blue, you don’t have a BE-7 engine, you don’t have the cryo tanks,” Creech said. “They’re representing the mass of the lander when it comes back from the surface because we think that’s the most critical case. But it does have the crew cabin.”.

    It has been revealed that while there’s no Starship life support demonstration on Artemis III, NASA added a new milestone to SpaceX’s Moon lander contract to test parts of its crew cabin on the ground. The additional testing involves construction of a prototype crew compartment, called Cabin One, at SpaceX’s test site at Starbase, Texas.

    It has been revealed that NASA levied new test requirements on Blue Origin, too. The organization intends to launch its first Blue Moon test mission early next year after a monthslong delay caused by a rocket explosion on Blue Origin’s launch pad in May. This version of Blue Moon, known as Mark 1, has a single hydrogen-fueled BE-7 main engine. Future human-rated landers from Blue Origin will have three.

    “One of the things we added into the program in the last year is, we really felt like we needed a test of the three-engine configuration,” Creech remarked. The hotfire test of the three-engine Blue Moon propulsion unit will occur inside a vacuum chamber at NASA’s In-Space Propulsion Facility in Ohio.

    Sources indicate that this year’s Artemis shakeup did more than change the flight blueprint for Artemis III. Engineers also altered the architecture for subsequent lunar landing missions. The updated aims will make life easier for teams working on Starship and Blue Moon. That’s not necessarily the case for Orion.

    In a recent development, “Our previous architecture for both these landers required a 90-day loiter in lunar orbit for Orion to arrive,” Creech noted. “That was something that, for both of these landers, drove a lot of complexity, and a lot of it made the lander job really hard.”.

    The new concept of operations removes some of that complexity, according to NASA.

    According to recent reports, “One of the things we changed was that 90-day loiter,” Creech said. “SpaceX, they solved it by saying let’s do an Earth orbit rendezvous with Orion, and take Orion to the Moon. For both Blue Origin and SpaceX, we have updated their requirements to a four-day surface day initially. Before, our initial missions were six-and-a-half days.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the six-and-a-half-day surface stay was baked into the Artemis architecture because the Orion spacecraft was originally planned to settle into a long, looping path around the Moon, called a near-rectilinear halo orbit. This orbit was predicated by the expected location of NASA’s now-canceled Gateway lunar space station. That, in turn, was driven by Orion’s inability to reach an orbit closer to the Moon.

    In a recent development, now, instead of rendezvousing with Starship near the Moon on landing missions, Orion will link up with Starship in high-Earth orbit. From there, Starship will propel it toward the Moon.

    In a recent development, what’s still unclear, however, is whether SpaceX will have to refuel Starship at an altitude above low-Earth orbit. A graphic presented by Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, last month illustrated this possibility with a “final tanking orbit” before Starship docks with Orion in high-Earth orbit.

    “We’re still working that out,” Creech said. “We’re making progress, but where we actually rendezvous with Orion is still in trade, so that’s why you saw a little bit of fuzziness there.”.

    It has been revealed that for missions using Blue Moon, the lander will connect with Orion in orbit around the Moon. Blue Origin’s updated plans do away with the requirement for in-space refueling but will still require four launches of the manufacturer’s Fresh Glenn rocket, one for the Blue Moon lander itself and three with transfer stages to boost it out of Earth orbit to the Moon.

    According to recent reports, A fresh stretched Centaur upper stage for the Space Launch System should give the rocket energy to send Orion to low-lunar orbit, which it could not reach with the current version of SLS. NASA has not determined if the new Centaur exploration stage will be ready in time for Artemis IV. If not, Artemis IV could fly with the last of NASA’s in-stock SLS upper stages.

    In a recent development, NASA is also waiting to decide which lander to use on Artemis IV. In either case, two of Orion’s four astronauts will transfer into the landers for the final descent to the lunar surface for a four-day stay, then take off and return to Orion.

    Starship and Blue Moon must each complete an uncrewed landing demonstration before a crewed lunar mission. The landing demos are targeted for late 2027 or early 2028, Creech noted, but they won’t necessarily test everything crews will need when they head for the lunar south pole.

    In a recent development, starship’s elevator, for example, is not part of SpaceX’s uncrewed landing demonstration. Engineers will use a test lab at Marshall Space Flight Center in Alabama to check the elevator’s performance in a simulated lunar environment.

    In a recent development, NASA did not initially require SpaceX or Blue Origin to prove their landers could take off from the Moon before a crew mission. Government officials later added the lunar takeoff requirement for each tech giant’s uncrewed landing demos.

    It has been revealed that for now, NASA is leaving the details of the uncrewed takeoff demo up to SpaceX and Blue Origin. During Apollo, NASA’s lunar lander never landed on the Moon before Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin descended to the Sea of Tranquility. NASA did, however, fly a dress rehearsal around the Moon on Apollo 10 that included a test of the lunar module’s landing abort capability.

    Recent findings suggest that “Where we are today is, Blue will land and then do a full ascent back to the rendezvous point with Orion,” Creech mentioned. “With SpaceX. They will land, they will take off again, get to main stage on the engines, and then they will do another landing on the surface.”.

    That could change. Today’s initiative gives SpaceX two shots at proving Starship can safely land on the Moon, but it comes with trade-offs.

    In a recent development, “When I came into the program, I was like, ‘Why are we not going all the way to the rendezvous point?’” mentioned Creech, who took over as HLS program manager in 2025. “Some of my key people felt strongly we would get more out of the way we’re doing it now. There are others that have different opinions… We tend to have a lot of technical discussion and debate. That point will continue to be debated.”.

    It has been revealed that for Starship, orbital refueling remains the key to the Moon. SpaceX’s propellant transfer demonstration will involve two Starships, one debuted from Florida and another from Texas, docking together in low-Earth orbit and transferring a “meaningful” amount of propellant from one ship to the other, Creech remarked.

    “The first quarter of next year, we will see a long-awaited propellant transfer test from SpaceX, where they launch two Starships in pretty close proximity, actually dock, and transfer, we’re calling it a meaningful amount, of propellant,” Creech told Ars. “That is going to be a big learning point if they pull that off, because their architecture depends on propellant aggregation and multiple propellant flights.”.

    The propellant transfer test will mark the first time one spacecraft has offloaded a significant quantity of cryogenic propellants—in this case, methane and liquid oxygen—onto another vehicle in space. It is the culmination of decades of government and commercial research on cryogenic orbital refueling. The results will tell engineers how much of the propellant will be lost from boil-off during the transfer.

    That is one reason why there’s still so much ambiguity about how many Starship refueling tankers SpaceX will need to launch to give the Starship lunar lander enough gas to fly to the Moon. Without refueling, Starships are restricted to flights in low-Earth orbit.

    Recent findings suggest that the low end of the estimate for Starship tankers is six to eight refueling flights to support a Starship lunar mission. Those numbers come from Elon Musk, SpaceX’s founder and CEO, and fall below NASA’s own conservative planning figure of 20 refueling rolls out. Musk’s figures hinge on future Starship upgrades to reach the vehicle’s full potential. SpaceX’s goal is to get Starship’s lift capacity up to 100 to 200 metric tons of payload to low-Earth orbit. Today’s version of Starship, known as Starship V3, is still far short of 100 metric tons of payload capacity.

    For context, a Starship carries 1,600 metric tons of propellant with its tanks full. Refueling flights using future, fully optimized Starships might be able to fill those tanks with as few as six tankers. That is not the case today.

    According to recent reports, spaceX is working on a taller, heavier Starship called Starship V4. It will fly with nine Raptor engines, an upgrade over the six-engine variant flying today. In 2025, Musk said Starship V4’s first launch was targeted for 2027. There hasn’t been a recent upgrade to the schedule for Starship V4.

    The initial Artemis lunar missions will use Starship V3, Creech remarked.
